proof_skeleton_nl: First prove that K_{n,j} is antitone on the interval [0,1/n] by combining its differentiability on (0,1/n) with the fact that its derivative is nonpositive there. Then note that the theorem's hypothesis 0 ≤ d < 1/n puts both 0 and d inside that interval. Finally, apply antitone comparison to conclude K_{n,j}(d) ≤ K_{n,j}(0).

steps.trivial_justification: Combining differentiability on the open interval with the pointwise derivative bound gives exactly the input needed for the calculus monotonicity theorem.
